Exercise 15.7.23 — Volume of a Wedge: Setup and Exact Value

Problem. (a) Express the volume of the wedge in the first octant that is cut from the cylinder y2+z2=1y^2 + z^2 = 1y2+z2=1 by the planes y=xy = xy=x and x=1x = 1x=1 as a triple integral. (b) Use either the Table of Integrals or a computer algebra system to find the exact value of the triple integral in part (a).

Notation used in this solution

SymbolMeaning
dVdVdV Volume element. In the order we use, dV=dz dx dydV = dz\,dx\,dydV=dzdxdy.
cylinder y2+z2=1y^2 + z^2 = 1y2+z2=1 A right circular cylinder of radius 111 whose axis is the xxx-axis. In the first octant it keeps the points with y2+z2≤1y^2 + z^2 \leq 1y2+z2≤1.
wedge A solid cut out of a larger solid by two (or more) planes. Here the first-octant quarter of the cylinder is cut by the planes y=xy = xy=x and x=1x = 1x=1.
y=xy = xy=x A vertical plane through the zzz-axis. In the xyxyxy-plane it is the line from the origin at 45°, and it forms one side of the triangular cross section of the wedge.
CAS Computer algebra system. Part (b) uses SymPy, per the problem's instruction to use a CAS.

Part 1 — Express the volume as a triple integral

Step 1.1: Describe the wedge.

Work in the first octant (x,y,z≥0x, y, z \geq 0x,y,z≥0). The cylinder y2+z2=1y^2 + z^2 = 1y2+z2=1 limits the solid in the yzyzyz-directions: for each allowed yyy we have 0≤z≤1−y20 \leq z \leq \sqrt{1 - y^2}0≤z≤1−y2​. The two cutting planes determine the xxx-range. In the xyxyxy-plane the planes are the lines x=yx = yx=y and x=1x = 1x=1; between them, for 0≤y≤10 \leq y \leq 10≤y≤1, xxx runs from the line x=yx = yx=y to the plane x=1x = 1x=1:

0≤y≤1,y≤x≤1,0≤z≤1−y2. 0 \leq y \leq 1, \qquad y \leq x \leq 1, \qquad 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{1 - y^2}. 0≤y≤1,y≤x≤1,0≤z≤1−y2​.

The two planes meet each other along the line x=y=1x = y = 1x=y=1 (for all zzz) and meet the cylinder where y2+z2=1y^2 + z^2 = 1y2+z2=1. The plane x=1x = 1x=1 is the flat end cap of the wedge.

Step 1.2: Write the triple integral.

Integrating in zzz, then xxx, then yyy (volume element dV=dz dx dydV = dz\,dx\,dydV=dzdxdy):

Result of part (a). V=∫01∫y1∫01−y2dz dx dy. V = \int_0^1 \int_y^1 \int_0^{\sqrt{1-y^2}} dz\,dx\,dy. V=∫01​∫y1​∫01−y2​​dzdxdy.

Remark. The setup can be written in other orders as well; for instance, with xxx outermost, V=∫01∫0x∫01−y2dz dy dxV = \int_0^1 \int_0^x \int_0^{\sqrt{1-y^2}} dz\,dy\,dxV=∫01​∫0x​∫01−y2​​dzdydx. The expression above is the natural one, since the xxx-interval [y,1][y, 1][y,1] has constant length 1−y1 - y1−y before the zzz-integration.

Part 2 — Exact value by CAS (SymPy)

Step 2.1: Integrate the inner two integrals.

∫01−y2dz=1−y2,∫y11−y2 dx=(1−y)1−y2. \int_0^{\sqrt{1-y^2}} dz = \sqrt{1-y^2}, \qquad \int_y^1 \sqrt{1-y^2}\,dx = (1-y)\sqrt{1-y^2}. ∫01−y2​​dz=1−y2​,∫y1​1−y2​dx=(1−y)1−y2​.

Step 2.2: Reduce the remaining integral to a standard form.

V=∫01(1−y)1−y2 dy=∫011−y2 dy⏟(I)−∫01y1−y2 dy⏟(II). V = \int_0^1 (1-y)\sqrt{1-y^2}\,dy = \underbrace{\int_0^1 \sqrt{1-y^2}\,dy}_{\text{(I)}} - \underbrace{\int_0^1 y\sqrt{1-y^2}\,dy}_{\text{(II)}}. V=∫01​(1−y)1−y2​dy=(I)∫01​1−y2​dy​​−(II)∫01​y1−y2​dy​​.

(I) is a quarter of the unit disk: ∫011−y2 dy=π/4\int_0^1 \sqrt{1-y^2}\,dy = \pi/4∫01​1−y2​dy=π/4. For (II), substitute u=1−y2u = 1 - y^2u=1−y2, du=−2y dydu = -2y\,dydu=−2ydy:

∫01y1−y2 dy=12∫01u1/2 du=12⋅23 u3/2∣01=13. \int_0^1 y\sqrt{1-y^2}\,dy = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^1 u^{1/2}\,du = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{3}\,u^{3/2}\bigg|_0^1 = \frac{1}{3}. ∫01​y1−y2​dy=21​∫01​u1/2du=21​⋅32​u3/2​01​=31​.

Step 2.3: Combine.

V=π4−13. V = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{3}. V=4π​−31​.

Step 2.4: CAS verification (SymPy).

The script solution/part2_step1.py hands the exact integral ∫01 ⁣∫y1 ⁣∫01−y2dz dx dy\int_0^1 \!\int_y^1 \!\int_0^{\sqrt{1-y^2}} dz\,dx\,dy∫01​∫y1​∫01−y2​​dzdxdy to SymPy, which returns π/4−1/3\pi/4 - 1/3π/4−1/3. The same script also evaluates an independent order, ∫01 ⁣∫0x ⁣∫01−y2dz dy dx\int_0^1 \!\int_0^x \!\int_0^{\sqrt{1-y^2}} dz\,dy\,dx∫01​∫0x​∫01−y2​​dzdydx; both agree exactly, confirming the value.

Result of part (b). V=π4−13≈0.4521. V = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.4521. V=4π​−31​≈0.4521.

Step 2.5: Verification by Python (summary).

solution/part1_step1.py verifies the region description of Part 1 (the xxx-range at each yyy, and where the planes meet the cylinder). solution/part2_step1.py computes the exact value with SymPy in two independent orders and confirms π/4−1/3\pi/4 - 1/3π/4−1/3.
